en.title: Largest Ring with Adjacent Power Differences of at Most One
en.description:
Choose as many servers as possible and arrange them in a ring in any order so that the absolute power difference of every adjacent pair (including the first and last) is ≤1. Choosing just one server is allowed.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O, examples, and judging.
en.input: The first line contains n (1..200000), and the second line contains n power values (0..10⁹).
en.explanation: Example 1: choose 1, 1, 2, 2, 3 and arrange them as 1, 1, 2, 3, 2, for 5 servers; there is only one server with power 3, so the ring cannot cross over to 4 and come back. Example 2: each of the three values appears once, and the end values 1 and 3 differ by 2, so only 2 can be chosen. Example 3: two servers with the same value can both be chosen.
hints: The chosen distinct values must be consecutive, and every interior value other than the two end values must appear at least 2 times. Count the frequencies and scan consecutive keys: if the previous key has only 1 item, extending to a new key must restart from that previous key; otherwise, keep accumulating.
